body.heading: Fill your ocean
paragraphs: Ask your adult to help you fill a clear plastic bottle about one third full of water. Add a drop or two of blue food colouring and swirl it gently.
Slowly pour in cooking oil until the bottle is nearly full. Watch closely: the oil and the water do not mix. They stay in two layers.

body.heading: Make waves
paragraphs: Your adult screws the lid on tightly and checks it twice. Now tip the bottle slowly from side to side.
The blue water rolls and splashes like waves under the oil. Tip it gently for calm seas and a little faster for a storm. Put the bottle down if you want the sea to settle.

body.heading: Why they stay apart
paragraphs: Oil and water never mix, however hard you shake them. They always separate again, with the oil floating on top.
That is why rainbows can shine on puddles with oil in them, and why ducks' feathers stay dry. Oil and water like to keep to themselves.

description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: layer water and oil in a bottle and tip it to make rolling waves.

safetyNotes: An adult pours the oil, screws the lid on tightly, and checks it before any wave-making, so nothing spills.
Use a plastic bottle, never glass, and wipe up any spills straight away because oil makes floors slippery.
screenFreeExtension: Shake the bottle hard, then time how long the sea takes to become calm again; try to beat your own calm-down record.
takeaway: Oil and water always separate, and you can watch them do it.
